name: Coarse fabric with quartz temper
geological_formation: Casma valley fluvial sands derived from Cordillera Negra granodiorite
raw_material: Untreated alluvial clay with added river sand
description: Poorly sorted fabric with abundant (25–30%) angular to sub-angular monocrystalline quartz, 0.5–2.0 mm. Optically active reddish-brown matrix with common elongate voids. Consistent with low-temperature firing below 850 °C.
inclusion_kind: Monocrystalline quartz, plagioclase feldspar, rare hornblende
inclusion_size: Coarse sand to fine gravel (0.5–2.0 mm)

name: Fine orange paste
raw_material: Levigated kaolinitic clay, minimal added temper
description: Very fine, well-sorted fabric with sparse (<5%) silt-grade quartz in a highly birefringent kaolinitic matrix. Undifferentiated matrix birefringence indicates firing above 900 °C. The defining fabric of Thin Orange ware.
inclusion_size: Silt to very fine sand (<0.1 mm)

name: Volcanic temper with plagioclase
raw_material: Residual volcanic clay with crushed tuff temper
description: Fairly sorted fabric with 15–20% angular plagioclase laths, volcanic glass shards and rhyolitic rock fragments, 0.2–0.8 mm. Stipple-speckled matrix birefringence suggests moderate firing, roughly 750–850 °C.
inclusion_kind: Plagioclase, volcanic glass, rhyolite rock fragments

name: Calcareous fabric with crystalline calcite
raw_material: Marl clay with crushed calcite temper
description: Fairly sorted fabric with 20% cleaved crystalline calcite, 0.3–1.0 mm, in a carbonate-rich matrix. Micritic textural concentration features are common. Calcite survival indicates firing below roughly 750 °C.
inclusion_kind: Crystalline calcite, micritic limestone, rare quartz

name: Micaceous fabric
geological_formation: Weathered gneiss and schist, Valley of Oaxaca
raw_material: Alluvial clay from the Atoyac drainage
description: Well-sorted fabric with 10–15% muscovite and biotite laths aligned parallel to the vessel wall, plus sub-rounded quartz. Monostriated matrix birefringence indicates low compaction during forming.

name: Vesicular fabric with volcanic ash
raw_material: Fine clay with naturally occurring ash
description: Well-sorted fabric with abundant vesicles and 10% cuspate glass shards. Argillaceous clay fragments (ACFs) are frequent and sub-rounded, suggesting incomplete paste mixing. Optically inactive matrix indicates firing above 850 °C.
inclusion_kind: Cuspate volcanic glass shards, plagioclase, ACFs
